title: Compute brief - 19 November 2026
description: The money is there; the risk is moving down the stack. Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO on record while Nvidia tightened terms for neocloud guarantees and US transmission owners asked FERC for 10 to 20 year data centre contracts. Wire: Anthropic IPO, FERC grid contracts, Nvidia guarantees, LG Uplus Paju, Mega Or and Nebius, Salt Lake City ban, Jordan. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: Capital for the labs, take-or-pay for the builders.
lede: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 on 18 November, raising $81.3 billion, plus a $26 billion private placement at the same price, the largest offering on record; shares trade as ANT from today. The same day, Nvidia's quarterly filing showed up to $118 billion of infrastructure guarantees but new language that its neocloud commitments start only once those companies secure their own financing, and US transmission owners asked FERC to bind data centres to 10 to 20 year grid-upgrade contracts with collateral. Salt Lake City banned new data centres for 180 days a day after Loudoun's pause. Capital is flowing to the model labs; the long-dated risk is being pushed onto whoever builds and leases the megawatts. List prices held for a ninth day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69.
